summary.name: Maestro
summary.one_liner: Maestro is a desktop app for orchestrating multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode) so they can run autonomously on complex tasks, with phone check-ins.
use_cases: Running several AI coding agents in parallel on a codebase
Batch-processing markdown checklists with an agent overnight
Controlling agents from a phone while away from the desk
Scripting agent playbooks from cron or CI/CD via CLI
Browsing and resuming past Claude Code or Codex sessions
summary.what_it_does: Maestro is a desktop app that runs and manages multiple AI coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and OpenCode, in parallel, each with its own workspace and history. Its Auto Run feature lets agents work autonomously for hours by batch-processing markdown checklists and repeatable playbooks. It includes Git integration (repo detection, diff viewer, commit logs, worktrees for parallel runs on isolated branches), session discovery to browse and resume past conversations, and a full CLI for headless operation. A built-in web server with QR code access lets you control agents from a phone, locally or via Cloudflare tunnel, and SSH support runs agents on remote hosts.
notable: Event-driven Maestro Cue automation triggered by file changes, timers, GitHub activity, or agent completion (off by default)
Session discovery across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and OpenCode sessions
Mobile remote control via built-in web server with QR code and Cloudflare tunnel
Listed as open source on GitHub (pedramamini/Maestro) per the awesome-mac listing
caveats: Many Encore features are only in the release candidate and require enabling beta updates in Settings
Maestro Cue is off by default and must be turned on in Settings
Pricing is not stated on the page
